question.leadin: Answer some questions about mink in history.
question.text: This president claimed that his wife, Pat, "doesn't have a mink coat" in his "Checkers" speech. This man was later forced to resign over the Watergate scandal, despite declaring "I am not a crook".
question.clue: A ruling in which this man was the respondent cited Accardi v. Shaughnessy to assert the power of the Attorney General and notes that "in camera inspection" is not a substantial diminishment of communications.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about advancements in space exploration.
swap.text: The first American human spaceflight program shared its name with this planet, the closest planet to the Sun.
swap.clue: The number 7 featured in the names of every vehicle used, including Friendship 7, flown by John Glenn, and Freedom 7, flown by Alan Shepard, the first American in space.

question.text: In both the 1952 and 1956 Presidential elections, Eisenhower defeated this man to win the election. This former Illinois Governor was the grandson of a former US Vice President under Grover Cleveland.
question.clue: The grandson of the 23rd U.S Vice-President, in 1948 he was elected governor of .

swap.leadin: B-26 bombers were repainted to look like FAR planes to maintain the illusion that this event was operated only by rebel troops.
swap.text: Name this failed 1961 invasion that attempted to overthrow the Communist dictator of Cuba.
swap.answerHtml: Bay of Pigs invasion (accept Operation Zapata; accept word forms for invasion)
swap.clue: This event's failure led Allen Dulles to be forced to resign.

question.text: After the invasion, the US passed a bill named for Nichols and this politician to reduce inter-service rivalry. Reagan spoke in support of this conservative politician at the 1964 RᐧNᐧC in the speech "A Time for Choosing".
question.clue: He was harmed by a message which ended "We must love one another, or we must die" after zooming in on the eye of a figure who skips the number six and repeats the number nine twice in trying to count to ten.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about United States international diplomacy during the presidencies of Nixon and Ford.
swap.text: Most of the diplomatic stance of their presidencies was shaped by this National Security Advisor and Secretary of State under both presidents. He won the Nobel Peace Prize for the Paris Peace Accords alongside Le Duc Tho.
swap.clue: This man, who may have coordinated the assassination of Archbishop Makarios, coined the term "constructive ambiguity" to describe his policy toward China.

question.leadin: Name these Secretaries of State of the United States of America.
question.text: This Secretary of State under Eisenhower refused to shake Zhou Enlai's hand and was a major player in overthrowing Guatemalan President Jacobo Arbenz in Operation PBSUCCESS.
question.clue: This politician's brother oversaw the MK Ultra program as CIA director until he was forced to resign following the Bay of Pigs Invasion.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about famous pictures of tanks.
swap.text: One advertisement against this man featured footage of him riding in a tank and listed his foreign-policy stances, including his opposition to the Pershing II missiles, and said that America "couldn't afford [the] risk" of his being president.
swap.clue: Judge Shira Scheindlin repeatedly ruled against the tactics of his police.

question.leadin: At the time of his rise to prominence, he was being investigated for taking bribes from Pepsi-Cola.
question.text: Identify this Wisconsin senator who won election in 1946 after smearing a nearly fifty-year-old opponent for not enlisting in World War II.
question.clue: This man succeeded Robert La Follette, Jr. in his highest ranking position, and he also chaired the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

swap.text: While many Republicans held back from supporting Goldwater, Ronald Reagan gave this speech in support of him a week before the election. Known often just as "The Speech," it propelled Reagan into national prominence.
swap.clue: It was known as "The Speech" while being perfected over a series of deliveries to city Chambers of Commerce, before it was finally delivered on television by the host of GE Theater.

question.leadin: In 1972 the Democratic National Committee had its headquarters on the sixth floor of this building. FTPE.
question.text: What Washington DC hotel lent its name to a scandal first involving the wiretapping of those DNC offices?
question.clue: Carl Bernstein and Bob Woodward reported on the events in this building.

swap.text: The Newdow case concerned whether this two-word phrase in the Pledge of Allegiance violated the Establishment Clause, since it refers to a specific Christian figure.
swap.clue: Because John Nicolay and John Hay's drafts omit this phrase, some people are skeptical that this two-word phrase was used before the words "shall have a new birth of freedom" in the last sentence of the Gettysburg Address.

question.text: Although Shockley was a terrible boss, he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Bardeen and Walter Brattain for inventing these devices.

swap.leadin: The United States' judicial system has seen plenty of odd defenses used by defendants. answer some questions about them.
swap.text: This defense was used by Dan White after the murders of Harvey Milk and George Moscone. His lawyers argued that he suffered from depression caused by a change in diet to the namesake sugary treat.

question.leadin: Name these major players in the Cuban Missile Crisis.
question.text: This Secretary of Defense under John F. Kennedy supported the naval blockade that was America's first response to reports of missiles being sent to Cuba.
question.clue: He served as a member of EXCOMM during the Cuban Missile Crisis and persuaded the Joint Chiefs of Staff to choose the blockade option over a missile strike.

swap.leadin: William Safire was a speechwriter for this President.
swap.text: Name this President whom Safire had previously worked for in his failed 1960 presidential campaign. Safire coined the phrase "nattering nabobs of negativism" for this man's Vice-President, Spiro Agnew.

question.text: During the 1947 HUAC hearings on Hollywood, this screenwriter testified that the film Song of Russia was Communist propaganda. This witness claimed that the film misrepresented life in the Soviet Union, where "human life is nothing, less than nothing."

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the VENONA Project, a US-UK joint effort to decode encrypted Soviet cables.
swap.text: The cables led to the arrest and eventual execution of this couple, accused of passing nuclear secrets on to the Soviets through a Los Alamos machinist named David Greenglass.
swap.clue: Kaufman was the judge in the 1951 trial of this couple for passing nuclear secrets to the Soviet Union. He proclaimed their crime was "worse than murder" after their conviction.

question.text: During 1968, this so-called "Dragon Lady" arranged secret discussions between the leadership of South Vietnam and Nixon, who encouraged them to pull out of scheduled peace talks to get a better deal from the Nixon administration.
question.clue: This woman who passed on a message from Richard Nixon to the South Vietnamese to hold out for a better deal during negotiations of the Paris Peace Accords. She became a leading figure in the "China Lobby" after marrying the founder of the Flying Tigers.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about immigration legislation in the US, FTPE.
swap.text: This Senator hated the New Deal, Communists, and foreigners despite being the son of Irish immigrants. With Francis Walter, he co-sponsored a 1952 piece of legislation that revised the immigration quota system and allowed for the deportation of immigrants for subversive activities.
swap.clue: After Tydings' defeat, most of the members of the Tydings Committee worked for a similar committee named for this Nevada Democrat, the namesake and sponsor of the 1950 Internal Security Act passed over Truman's veto.
